items.question_text: A 80-year-old man has critical ischaemia and is unfit. What is discussed? He is otherwise as described and no other finding is present. Pulses and the limb are as stated. The rest of the history does not create an exception. Apply the vascular decision to the facts in front of you. Do not discharge or delay on a workaround. State the correct step. Document the assessment, the rule, and the action. The Australian guidance is the same in any hospital. Apply it to the facts already given. That is the priority. Nothing else changes the first correct step. A palpable pulse elsewhere does not clear an ischaemic limb already present. Apply it and do not wait. Do that now. Age and a busy list do not change the pathway. He can speak and has no chest pain. A relative wants him discharged. That does not change the vascular priority. Apply the guidance and document the decision. Do not wait for the limb to worsen. The finding already present is the indication to act.
